names_for.catalogue_side: Adobe Stock (licensed 'Stock Assets' under Standard, Enhanced and Extended licences)

operator_role.note: Adobe sublicenses contributors' Work to buyers under its own User Agreement; contributors are not principals behind an agency.

economics_model.note: Contributors get 33% (images) or 35% (video); Adobe keeps the rest.

who_pays_fee.note: No buyer-side fee; Adobe's share comes out of the licence price before the contributor royalty.

supply_models.note: Only contributor uploads evidenced; whether Adobe also licenses whole collections from partner agencies was not established.

custody_model.note: Buyers download files; Adobe advises downloading because re-download may not be available after termination.

transaction_mode.note: Self-serve credit plans for individuals; phone and consultation for teams and enterprise.

public_prices.note: Individual plans and credit costs are published; enterprise pricing goes through a consultation.

licence_model.note: Standard, Enhanced and Extended licences (plus Editorial and Comp).

exclusivity_offered.note: Adobe's own right to sublicense is non-exclusive, so no exclusive licence can be offered.

versioning.note: Single assets, not versioned datasets; nothing published on revisions.

human_subject_consent_docs.note: Contributor warrants releases and gives them to Adobe on request; buyers get an indemnity (capped) rather than release copies.

contributor_pay_model.note: Per-licence royalties plus a discretionary annual Firefly training bonus weighted by assets considered for training and the licences they earned.

catalogue_plus_custom.note: No custom or commissioned service found; the business product page timed out, so this rests on the 10-K description and the pages fetched.

erasure_after_sale.note: Buyers must cease use and possession if Adobe instructs them over a suspected third-party claim; a contributor's own removal does not reach licences already sold.

Q1.answer: Designers and businesses license single assets through credit plans (10 to 750 credits a month) and in-app from Photoshop, Illustrator and Express; video costs more credits than images. Buyer terms forbid using assets to train AI, so it is not a training-data source for buyers; volumes and buyer mix are not published.

Q2.answer: Contributors get distribution into Adobe's apps (Stock, Firefly, Express, Creative Cloud) and to API partners and affiliates, with no API of their own; Adobe gives no reason a contributor would list here rather than sell directly.

Q3.answer: Inventory comes from contributor uploads under a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free licence to Adobe that also covers 'developing new features and services'; Adobe trains Firefly on licensed content and pays contributors a discretionary annual training bonus based on assets considered for training and the licences they earned.

Q4.answer: No commissioned work is resold. Contributor terms reach Work uploaded under earlier versions, and contributors accept new pricing simply by not removing their Work; Adobe's training use rests on a general 'new features and services' clause, compensated by a discretionary bonus. Contributor reaction to the training use was not researched (no search).

Q5.answer: Adobe is licensor of record: it sublicenses under its own User Agreement and is not the contributor's agent. Contributors warrant rights and releases and indemnify buyers; Adobe also indemnifies buyers of paid, non-editorial assets up to US$10,000 per asset.

Q6.answer: Assets are downloaded by the buyer (web or API); Adobe hosts the files and advises buyers to download licensed assets because re-download may not be available after termination.

Q7.answer: Contributors warrant model and property releases and hand them to Adobe on request; editorial work may go without releases. Buyers can filter for released assets but are not shown to receive the releases; Adobe's indemnity covers publicity and privacy claims, and use for identifying people is banned.

Q8.answer: Non-exclusive tiered licences (Standard with a 500,000 cap, Enhanced, Extended); no resale of licences and a ban on AI training and face identification. Adobe can order a buyer to cease use and possession of an asset facing a claim, but enforcement against infringers is at Adobe's option; no audit or fingerprinting terms found.

Q9.answer: Self-serve credit subscriptions and packs with published prices, plus a consultation route and an enterprise-only API for businesses. Adobe owns the licence relationship and pays contributors a 33% (images) or 35% (video) royalty.

Q10.answer: The unit is a single Stock Asset licensed to a user or business; licences are perpetual and survive a subscription ending or the asset's removal, while Adobe may stop licensing any asset. No dataset or revision object exists.

Q11.answer: Buyers can download watermarked comp versions for 90 days of preview use; the API exposes release and AI-generated flags. Adobe disclaims the accuracy of assets and their metadata.

Q12.answer: Only a catalogue side was found ('Adobe Stock', licensed 'Stock Assets'); Adobe's annual report describes a library and no custom collection service. The business product page timed out, so a custom offer cannot be ruled out.

unknowns.note: stock.adobe.com returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch for the homepage, search and asset pages (only /plans and /license-terms loaded), so no real listing could be opened to see what an anonymous buyer sees.
Terms describe subscription accounts and restrict API access to enterprise customers, but no page says what Adobe checks about a buyer before a self-serve licence.
Items are single assets; nothing published on replacing or revising an asset after sale.

Adobe calls the collection 'curated' in its 10-K and disclaims accuracy of metadata, but the submission-review guidelines on helpx.adobe.com returned 403, so operator review of submissions is not evidenced.
The Adobe Stock business page timed out three times; whether Adobe offers custom shoots or collections to enterprise buyers is unconfirmed.
The 10-K gives no Adobe Stock revenue, asset count beyond 'millions', contributor count or bonus total.
Reports that Adobe bought video from contributors per minute for Firefly training (2024) could not be looked for without web search.
